precepts.text: The tabernacle was set up at Shiloh, in Ephraim.
precepts.point: Joseph saved Israel in the famine and Joshua of Ephraim divided the land. Ephraim therefore felt more entitled than Judah, and the rivalry began long before the split.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
“And the whole congregation of the children of Israel assembled together at Shiloh, and set up the tabernacle of the congregation there. And the land was subdued before them.” From there each tribe received its allotment of land.

On the map, the hill country of Ephraim holds Shiloh, Ai, Shechem at the top, and Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal, where the law’s blessings and curses were received. Bethlehem and Jerusalem lie further down, in Judah. All of Israel’s earliest places of worship were in Ephraim’s land: Abraham’s first altar at Shechem, Bethel, the mountains of the law, and the tabernacle at Shiloh.

So Ephraim felt entitled. They had the places of worship, the historical landmarks, and they were more in number than Judah. That is where the beef started, the buildup of the dividing hatred.

It broke open with Rehoboam. “And Rehoboam went to Shechem: for all Israel were come to Shechem to make him king”, crowned at the very place of Abraham’s first altar. Solomon had laid a heavy yoke of taxes on the people to build sanctuaries of heathen worship for his wives. The old men who had served with Solomon said, lift it and they will serve you forever; Rehoboam “forsook the old men’s counsel” and listened to the young men he grew up with: “my father also chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.” It was so “for the cause was from the Lord”, to fulfill what Ahijah the Shilonite told Jeroboam when he tore the garment into twelve pieces and gave him ten.

Israel answered, “What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David.” They stoned Rehoboam’s tax collector, and made Jeroboam king. Only Judah, with Benjamin at its side, followed the house of David. When Rehoboam gathered an army, the Lord said, do not fight your brethren, “for this thing is from me.” The split was the Lord’s doing, and its roots ran back to the land at Shiloh.

precepts.text: The hand of the diligent shall bear rule, but the slothful shall be under tribute; the other tribes were diligent and went and conquered their land.
precepts.point: We cannot sit back knowing Christ is coming and not do the work; the time is short, and this is not our rest. We have to bring our brothers and sisters to repentance.

note.label: Joshua 18: The Lots Cast at Shiloh

precepts.why:
“How long are ye slack to go to possess the land, which the Lord God of your fathers hath given you?” The land was already given; they were waiting instead of going in to possess it. Slack means lazy, slothful, full of excuses. “The hand of the diligent shall bear rule: but the slothful shall be under tribute.” The other tribes were diligent and went and conquered their land; the slothful sit and wait.

It is the same spirit a lot of our brothers and sisters have today: you have gifts you bring to the table, but you exercise them for your boss at work and are slack when it comes to the necessities of your nation. This shows we are the children of Israel, because that is the spirit we have, and we have to come out of that thing.

precepts.text: Be in pain and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion; the daughter of Zion is the children of Israel.
precepts.point: We cannot sit back knowing Christ is coming and not do the work; the time is short, and this is not our rest. We have to bring our brothers and sisters to repentance.

note.label: Joshua 18: The Lots Cast at Shiloh

precepts.why:
“Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail”. The daughter of Zion is the children of Israel, and the word to her is labour. She shall go “even to Babylon; there shalt thou be delivered; there the Lord shall redeem thee from the hand of thine enemies.”

We cannot sit back knowing Christ is coming and not do the work; the time is short, and this is not our rest. The slack spirit of Joshua 18 has to go: we have to be in pain and labour to bring our brothers and sisters to repentance.

precepts.text: The kingdom of God is within you; it is up to us to labour and bring forth the kingdom.
precepts.point: We cannot sit back knowing Christ is coming and not do the work; the time is short, and this is not our rest. We have to bring our brothers and sisters to repentance.

note.label: Joshua 18: The Lots Cast at Shiloh

precepts.why:
“Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you.” The kingdom is not something to sit and wait for somewhere else; it is within us, so it is up to us to labour and bring it forth.

That is the answer to “How long are ye slack”. The land was given and they had to go possess it; the kingdom of God is within you and you have to do the work, bringing our brothers and sisters to repentance while the time is short.

precepts.text: The lot is cast into the lap, but the whole disposing thereof is of the Lord; the Lord decided the outcome of the inheritance of these lands.
precepts.point: The description of the seven parts was to be brought to Joshua, that he may cast lots for them before the Lord. Casting lots is like throwing dice or drawing straws: you may be the one throwing, but the Lord decides what comes up.

note.label: Joshua 18: The Lots Cast at Shiloh

precepts.why:
Joshua says to describe the land into seven parts and bring it to him, “that I may cast lots for you here before the Lord our God.” Casting lots is like throwing dice or drawing straws: you may be the one throwing, but the Lord decides what comes up. “The lot is cast into the lap; but the whole disposing thereof is of the Lord.”

So the inheritance of these lands was not Joshua's choosing. The lot was cast before the Lord, and the Lord decided the outcome of who received what.

precepts.text: The mariners said, Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil is upon us; they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah, because the lot belongs to the Lord.
precepts.point: The description of the seven parts was to be brought to Joshua, that he may cast lots for them before the Lord. Casting lots is like throwing dice or drawing straws: you may be the one throwing, but the Lord decides what comes up.

note.label: Joshua 18: The Lots Cast at Shiloh

precepts.why:
Jonah is also the picture of the slack spirit Joshua is speaking to. The word of the Lord came to him, “Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it”, but Jonah wanted nothing to do with prophesying to wake his people up: he “rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the Lord”, paid the fare and went down into the ship. The Lord sent out a great wind, “so that the ship was like to be broken”, and while the mariners cried every man unto his god and cast the wares into the sea, “Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.” The shipmaster had to wake him: “What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God”.

America is that spiritual ship that is going to sink, and a lot of our people are asleep in the middle of the chaos, comfortable while a pestilence from the Lord is on the earth.

Then the lot: “Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil is upon us. So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.” It fell on Jonah because the lot belongs to the Lord; the whole disposing of it is his, the same way the lots Joshua cast for the seven parts of the land were decided by the Lord.

precepts.text: The Levites do the service of the tabernacle, and among the children of Israel they have no inheritance.
precepts.point: The Levites have no part among you, for the priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance. The Levites were well taken care of; they dwelt in the suburbs of the cities and had the best of everything.

note.label: Joshua 18: The Lots Cast at Shiloh

precepts.why:
“But the Levites have no part among you; for the priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance”. That was set long before: “But the Levites shall do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation, and they shall bear their iniquity: it shall be a statute for ever throughout your generations, that among the children of Israel they have no inheritance.”

The Levites do the service of the tabernacle, and that is their portion. It is a statute for ever, so no lot was cast for Levi among the seven parts. And the Levites were well taken care of; they dwelt in the suburbs of the cities and had the best of everything.

precepts.text: Levi hath no part nor inheritance with his brethren; the Lord is his inheritance.
precepts.point: The Levites have no part among you, for the priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance. The Levites were well taken care of; they dwelt in the suburbs of the cities and had the best of everything.

note.label: Joshua 18: The Lots Cast at Shiloh

precepts.why:
“Wherefore Levi hath no part nor inheritance with his brethren; the Lord is his inheritance, according as the Lord thy God promised him.” This is why Joshua says the Levites have no part among you: the Lord himself is Levi's inheritance, and the priesthood of the Lord is his portion, according as it was promised.

Gad, Reuben and the half tribe of Manasseh had already received theirs beyond Jordan on the east from Moses, and Levi's was the Lord; so the seven parts were for the seven tribes that remained.
